time.desc: A trade agreement was announced: import tariffs on a major trading partner were lowered to levels lower than previously threatened, in exchange for the other party's commitment to large-scale investment and market opening.

The initiating country reached a trade agreement with a long-term ally, lowering the country's import tariffs from previously threatened levels. The other party promised to invest heavily in the initiating country and open its market, while also lowering auto tariffs.

The two major economies confirmed their agreement to extend the tariff truce. The financial chief of the sponsoring country said that the other party's representatives were "a little too hasty" and said that the leaders will make a final decision within two weeks.

The executive order cancels tariff exemptions for low-value packages in advance and globally, and at the same time announces the imposition of high tariffs on some copper semi-finished products and sets a time for the imposition of tariffs in the near future.

The sponsoring country signed an executive order to cancel the tariff exemption for low-value packages in advance and globally, so that small-value packages are taxed at the rate of the country of origin.
The sponsoring country announced that it will impose a 50% tariff on some semi-processed metal products and will take effect soon. After the announcement, the metal futures plummeted by nearly 20%.

The federal appeals court held a hearing and questioned the legality of the president's emergency authorization to impose large-scale tariffs; at the same time, a new round of "reciprocal tariffs" took effect as planned.

The federal appeals court held a hearing on the legality of the president's emergency authorization to impose large-scale tariffs and put pressure on government lawyers, just one day before reciprocal tariffs were scheduled to take effect.
The sponsoring country's new round of 'reciprocal' tariffs will officially take effect within a set period, covering dozens of countries, with tax rates ranging from 10% to 40%

A major country in the southern hemisphere was levied an additional 40% tariff due to the trial of the former president, raising the total tax rate to 50%; an energy importing country was threatened with an additional 25% tariff and was given several weeks to respond.

Citing insufficient cooperation on border security and anti-drug cooperation, tariff rates were further raised on imported goods from neighboring countries. Bilateral tensions escalated, but negotiation channels were still emphasized.
The sponsoring country raised the tariff on imported goods from a neighboring country from 25% to 35% on the grounds of insufficient anti-drug cooperation.

The ambassador and chief negotiator of a neighboring country to the sponsoring country responded that this week's dialogue was professional and constructive, and pointed out that the exemption of goods that comply with existing agreements puts the country in a better position than most countries

The ruling party announced the implementation of a package of punitive tariffs on many countries, covering steel, aluminum, automobiles, agricultural products, etc., ranging from poor small countries to wealthy partners.
A central bank keeps its benchmark interest rate unchanged due to economic uncertainty caused by tariffs

For the first time, the foreign affairs department of an energy-importing country has publicly criticized the sponsoring country's tariff threat as "unfair and unreasonable" and countered that the other country is still trading with the conflicting party.

It announced the imposition of extremely high tariffs on semiconductors and the establishment of an exemption and traceability mechanism for "building factories/committing to build factories locally". At the same time, additional punitive tariffs on goods from an important economy significantly increased the total tax rate.

The sponsoring country officially announced the imposition of extremely high tariffs on semiconductors and the establishment of an exemption for local factory construction and a recovery mechanism for unfulfilled duties.

The initiating country formally imposed an additional 2.5% tariff on an energy importing country, raising the total tax rate to 50%. The country responded by calling the move 'unfair, unreasonable, and without justifiable reasons.'

The authorities of a technology-producing area submitted formal opinions to the sponsoring country on semiconductor tariffs and sought exemptions, warning that tax increases would increase business costs and reduce investment willingness.

The 20% tariff imposed by the sponsoring country on goods from a certain technological origin has officially come into effect, affecting the export of machine tools, plastic products and agricultural products.
